author: worker-1
text:
The vulnerable program’s `fread` reads at most 64 bytes into `buf[64]`, so `n` can never exceed 64. The check `if (n > 77)` is therefore unreachable, and `abort()` cannot be triggered by any file content. The “fixed” version only prints the byte count and also cannot crash. This suggests the supplied `vuln.c` does not contain the described length-overflow bug, or the relevant check/input path is missing from the snippet.

I would next inspect `submit.sh` to see how it invokes the binaries and interprets JSON, and test with trivial files (empty, 64 bytes) to confirm both exit 0. I would also verify whether the actual compiled target matches this source rather than assuming it does.
